description: A 3-pin SPDT (single-pole double-throw) switch: pin 2 (common) is always connected to either pin 1 or pin 3, depending on the handle position.
how_to_use: Pin 2 (the middle one) is the common terminal. Slide the handle toward pin 1 and pins 1+2 are joined; slide it toward pin 3 and pins 2+3 are joined. It stays where you put it — an on/off switch. For a simple on/off, wire the middle pin and ONE end pin, and leave the other end unconnected. Pins 1 and 3 aren't interchangeable: swapping them swaps which position is 'on'.

pins.1: one end — joined to the middle pin when the handle is slid toward pin 1
pins.2: the middle (common) pin — always joined to pin 1 or pin 3
pins.3: the other end — joined to the middle pin when the handle is slid toward pin 3
